name: Water where it shouldn't be
cause: A failed supply line or a pinhole in an old copper pipe, usually under a sink or behind the washer.
fix: Shut the water, find the source, replace the failed section, and pressure-test the line.

name: A drain that won't drain
cause: Grease, hair or wipes built up past the trap. One slow drain is a local clog; several means the main line.
fix: Clear it with a cable from the nearest cleanout, run water for ten minutes, and show you the camera if you want it.

name: No hot water
cause: On a gas heater, a worn thermocouple or pilot. On electric, a burnt-out element or thermostat.
fix: Test the part, replace it from the van, and flush the tank while we're there. We only quote a new heater if the tank is leaking.

name: A toilet that runs or rocks
cause: A tired flapper or fill valve if it runs; a broken wax seal or flange if it rocks.
fix: Rebuild the tank, or lift the toilet, replace the seal and bolts, and reset it level.

name: Weak pressure everywhere
cause: A failing pressure regulator at the meter, or galvanized pipes narrowed by decades of scale.
fix: Gauge the pressure at the hose bib, replace the regulator, or quote a repipe in writing if the pipes are the cause.
